invalid_inference_schemes.invalid_inference: A shared inflection/derivational string is sufficient to prove a shared lexical root
Any internal substring crossing boundaries is a lexical component
Equal lossy search forms prove equal native lexemes or senses
safe_automatic, compound_morphology or manually_verified is independent lexical gold

patterns.reason: The sequence gup is mainly the boundary between an English verb ending in g and the separate particle up (bringing up, going up), mixed with unrelated names and concatenated text. No shared whole-lemma etymology connects the list.
The repeated letters rrt occur in unrelated misspellings and onomatopoeia (chart, heart, court, start, and others); they are not an etymological stem.
The sequence mef crosses unrelated concatenated words (came from, me feel, me for), names, and spelling errors; it is not a common whole-word root.
Repeated nnn is a transcription elongation or coincidental spelling in unrelated names and phrases; it is not an etymological stem of the whole entries.
The sequence dib occurs in unrelated personal names, foreign words, text glued together and playful spellings; the list shares no whole-word etymology.
The three-letter transliterated sequence abr collects unrelated Russian fragments, surnames and words including чабрец and взабрать; it does not identify a whole-word etymological family.
The nni sequence combines unrelated names, transliterations and fragments, and does not attest a common whole-word origin.
The cil sequence is shared by otherwise unrelated surnames, foreign words, chemical names and corpus fragments; it is not a common whole-word etymology.
The transliterated esb sequence occurs in different names, malformed forms and joins such as оставайтесб; it does not connect the whole entries etymologically.
The short sequence ofn is an abbreviation or a coincidental sequence crossing unrelated words and concatenated corpus fragments; the list has no common whole-word etymology.
The sequence lpo crosses unrelated components in point, polish, poetry, politics and proper names; the token lpo is not evidence of their shared etymology.
The apparent ilv component joins unrelated names, spelling errors and words such as happily/heavily; it is not a shared lexical root of the whole entries.
-rla spans unrelated Spanish verbs followed by the clitic la, including abandonarla, abrirla and visitarla; matching this ending is not a shared lexical origin.
-ado is a common Spanish participial/adjectival ending, present in unrelated words such as abandonado, figurado and financiado; it is not their shared root.
-are is the Italian infinitive ending shared by unrelated verbs such as abbandonare, macellare and zufolare, not a common whole-word etymon.
-nos frequently represents an attached Spanish pronoun on unrelated verbs, such as abandonarnos, abatirnos and garantícenos; other words coincidentally end in the same letters.
-ría often marks the Spanish conditional or noun formation; unrelated words such as abandonaría, imprimiría and zapatería do not form one lexical family.
Transliterated -vat matches the final part of -вать/-овать/-ировать in unrelated Russian verbs, including адаптировать, подогревать and подлизывать; this ending does not establish a common stem.
The transliterated -yj is the recurring Russian adjective ending -ый/-ий, visible in unrelated adjectives such as должный, самый, нужный and главный; it is not a shared lexical etymon.
The transliterated -sja is the Russian reflexive suffix -ся/-сь shared by unrelated verbs including являться, собираться and нравиться; it is not their common whole-word root.
The transliterated -skij is the Russian adjectival ending -ский in unrelated words such as российский, женский and японский; a common suffix is not a common lexical family.
The transliterated -nie frequently reflects the Russian noun ending -ние in unrelated words such as отношение, решение and внимание; it is not one shared stem.
German -nen often crosses verb endings and unrelated stems, as in warnen, begegnen and regnen, and does not justify grouping the full words by origin.

The transliterated surface sequence ka groups unrelated Russian stems and endings. Examples include абиссинийка (nationality), аэрофотосъёмка (recording), адвокатишка (diminutive/pejorative) and актрисочка (diminutive). The final letters -ка or -очка do not establish a shared whole-lemma etymon. Every stored link is candidate-index evidence rather than a checked lexical derivation.

Spanish -ote / -ándote groups unrelated verb forms with attached te, e.g. abalanzándote and zurrándote; no shared lexical root.
Russian -нуть is a productive infinitive ending on unrelated verbs, including хортонуть, отчеркнуть and прибухнуть.
French -tes matches unrelated plural or inflected words such as abates, importantes, procaryotes and zuchettes.
German -eln matches unrelated verbs and nominal plurals, including abbetteln, filterregeln, hobeln and urwaldregeln.
Russian -ность forms abstract nouns from unrelated bases, such as диалектичность, небрежность and тривиальность.
German -eren/-ieren is a verb ending and string overlap among unrelated stems, such as explizieren, pervertieren and transkribieren.
Spanish -ento/-miento matches unrelated nouns, verbs and noisy strings such as aplanamiento, entrtenimiento and revolcamiento.
Russian -ческий forms adjectives from distinct stems, e.g. абиотический, метаболический and статистический.
Spanish -amos is a first-person plural verb ending shared by unrelated verbs such as ignorabamos, nalgueamos and sociabilizamos.
Spanish -ras/-rás is an inflectional/string ending shared by unrelated forms such as abadonarás, captoras and supondras.
Adjectives from unrelated Russian stems share -тный; the exact corpus word тный is not a lexical root.
Spanish participles of unrelated verbs share -ido; idó and ído are spelling noise, not a common stem.
Unrelated plurals, names and concatenations end in ons; the isolated ons does not establish shared etymology.
Nouns from unrelated stems share the productive -ство ending; standalone ство/ьство is suffix material.
Unrelated infinitives plus first-person clitic -mi produce -armi; no single lexical root armi connects them.
Unrelated plurals and nationality names end in ans; standalone ans is not evidence for a common family.

English-index -sky is a productive surname ending on unrelated people and places, e.g. dubrowsky, kopytovsky and zyuganovsky. Retain eight explicitly selected sky-base words; reject surname suffix and incidental strings.
Italian -ina is a feminine/diminutive suffix or final sequence joining unrelated roots, including ballerina, felpina and panzina.
Spanish -cia is a final nominal sequence across unrelated stems such as ciencia, impermanencia and reflectancia.
English -tes matches unrelated plural and inflected strings such as associates, payrates and zombettes.
English -ngs matches plural -ings and names from unrelated bases, including meetings, grapplings and reddings.
Transliterated -ija matches the Russian final sequence -ия across unrelated stems: аббревиация, абдукция, астропроекция, нация and оториноларингология do not share a whole-lemma root.

Spanish final -elo includes attached pronouns on unrelated verbs (abandónelo, recógelo, comiéndoselo) alongside unrelated nouns such as abuelo and riachuelo; the shared ending is not a lexical family.
Italian -ato marks past participles and adjectives on unrelated stems: abbandonato, generalato, aranciato and telomerizzato do not derive from one lexical root.

The German -chen string is a diminutive suffix across unrelated nouns (Eulchen, Körperchen, Kügelchen), and also occurs in unrelated verb endings (coachen, schlichen) and compound/place names. A suffix match does not establish whole-lemma ancestry. The safe_automatic status was not supported by any checked etymology in these memberships.

The English final -ted includes unrelated participles such as dominated, protonated and exploited and hyphenated phrases such as media-related, along with corpus noise. It is not a common lexical root.
Spanish -ela joins pronouns to otherwise unrelated verbs (colocársela, mandándosela, recógertela) and also matches incidental final letters. It is not a shared whole-lemma etymon.

German -schen spans unrelated adjectives in -ischen (aquaristischen, enzymatischen, pyrokinetischen), diminutives and verbs (verramschen). It is not a common word root despite the safe_automatic status.
German -ers is a genitive or internal string in unrelated words such as Sprechers, Ferienlagers, Rinderserum and Trinkwassers; it is not a shared whole-word etymon.

German -ons and internal matching join unrelated surnames, borrowings and compounds such as Aarons, Informationsnachmittag, Polarisationsgerät and Zyklotrons. The final/internal letters do not imply one root.

Italian -elo commonly includes an attached object pronoun on unrelated verbs such as annotatelo, comunicatelo, puliscitelo and toglierglielo, while other words match incidentally. A clitic does not create one whole-lemma etymological family.
French final -ons spans unrelated first-person plural verbs (œuvrerons, ramènerons, restons) and nouns in -ions (suspensions, confessions). It is not a shared root.

Italian -mente is a productive adverbial suffix on unrelated adjective stems (avanzatamente, intrinsecamente, zoologicamente), not a shared whole-lemma etymon. The safe_automatic status did not represent individually verified origins.
German final -tes occurs in genitives and inflected adjectives from different stems (Baukonzeptes, degeneriertes, Stadtsenates, unausgereiftes).
Spanish -ose joins reflexive se to unrelated gerunds (beneficiándose, contradiciéndose, pinchándose) or matches incidental endings; it does not identify one lexical family.
Spanish -ando is a productive gerund ending on unrelated verbs (provisionando, revoleteando, examinando); it is not their common stem even where tagged safe_automatic.
English -ers joins unrelated plural agents, surnames and other words (homeschoolers, land-owners, petersburgers, twizzlers); it is not a shared lexical source.

Transliterated -vatsja matches the reflexive infinitive ending -ваться across unrelated verbs (эмитироваться, обёртываться, познаваться, совершенствоваться). It is not a common root despite safe_automatic status.
Spanish -arte attaches te to unrelated infinitives: abalanzarte, arañarte, disculparte, especializarte and zurrarte do not share a whole-lemma root.
Spanish -ias matches unrelated plurals, conditional forms and noisy strings such as apoplejias, contrarevolucionarias, derramarias and transferencias.
Spanish -ome mostly joins the reflexive/object pronoun me to unrelated gerunds, as in asegurándome, complicándome and molestándome.
Italian -ico is a productive adjectival ending on unrelated stems, including copulatico, idropneumatico, psicotico and stereochimico.
German -ken matches unrelated inflected words and compounds such as abbacken, Birkenweg, Erbsenpflücken and Zwischenbrücken.
Spanish -rio appears in unrelated nouns and adjectives such as abalorio, consultorio, equilibrio and otario; the ending is not their common lexical base.
Spanish -nes matches plural endings across unrelated stems (abalones, crayones, emociones, instituciones) and corpus noise.
Spanish -ito is a diminutive ending on unrelated words such as aaroncito, congeladito, huevito and ombliguito; it is not a shared root.
German -zen is a final or internal string spanning unrelated words such as abbeizen, raufzusetzen, Siedlungsplätzen and unterschätzen.
Transliterated -tyj joins unrelated Russian adjectives with final -тый, including криповатый, недомытый, расфуфыристый and corpus noise.
Spanish -ita is a feminine diminutive/final sequence joining unrelated stems such as abandonadita, birrita, manchita and taconita.
German -sen joins unrelated inflections and compounds such as Blumenblusen, Entschuldigungskeksen, Schwimmkursen and surnames.

German -ten is a frequent inflectional or stem-final sequence in unrelated words. The leading frequency words include berichten, kosten, richten, fürchten, antworten and verraten. All 17,618 materialized members have only candidate-index morphological evidence for this three-letter surface sequence; none has a documented direct etymological relation or manual override to the proposed whole-word family. Delete this incoherent association family while preserving the lemmas and their other family memberships.
